summary: The note summarizes the ethnic composition of Eritrea, which has nine recognized ethnic groups. According to SIL Ethnologue, Tigrayans make up about 50% of the population and the Tigre about 30%. Most remaining residents belong to other Afro-Asiatic-speaking Cushitic communities, with some Nilo-Saharan-speaking minorities and smaller groups.
one_line: Overview of Eritrea's nine recognized ethnic groups and their approximate population shares, per SIL Ethnologue.
key_facts: Eritrea has nine recognized ethnic groups.
According to SIL Ethnologue, Tigrayans make up about 50% of Eritrea's population.
According to SIL Ethnologue, the Tigre constitute around 30% of Eritrea's residents.
The Tigre speak a Semitic language.
Most of the rest of Eritrea's population belong to other Afro-Asiatic-speaking communities of the Cushitic branch.
Eritrea also has a number of Nilo-Saharan-speaking ethnic minorities.
Eritrea also has other smaller ethnic groups.
